quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, slow down and pull over to the side of the road. Stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, or a train is visible. If you are unsure whether a train is close enough to be dangerous, stop. Never try to race a train across the tracks.

questions.question: If you change your address, how must you notify the county examiner of drivers?
questions.explanation: You must notify the county examiner of drivers in writing within 30 days of changing your address. Include your new address, name, and driver license number.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided highway and see an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Disregard the signal if there are other lanes available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move your vehicle to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Increase your speed to get out of the way of the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your vehicle to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, slow down and move to provide a clear path. Stop your vehicle. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces your driving skills. It slows your reaction time and damages your judgment.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: When worn by the driver only.
When passengers wear them on long drives.
When all occupants wear them on expressways.
When all occupants wear them every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: When all occupants wear them every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. In a crash, an unbelted person becomes a flying object and can injure others in the vehicle.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to whom?
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash, stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check for injuries and call 911 if anyone is hurt. Report the crash to police if there are injuries, deaths, or damage over $1,000 to vehicles or $200 to government property.

questions.question: You must signal for at least ____ before turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: You must signal for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Signal for a longer distance when driving at higher speeds.

questions.question: What is a good way to stay alert on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips. If you get drowsy, pull off the road safely and take a nap or stay somewhere overnight.

questions.question: What affects braking distance?

options.text: The speed your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance is affected by your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you do?

options.text: Always signal, even when no other vehicles are visible.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even when no other vehicles are visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. This is the law and a safe habit.

questions.question: When towing a trailer that blocks your rearview mirror, you must:

options.text: Have an outside mirror on the driver's side only.
Have an outside mirror on the passenger's side only.
Have outside mirrors on both sides of your vehicle.
Have a person in the vehicle to help you turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have outside mirrors on both sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must have properly sized outside mirrors on both sides of your vehicle when towing a large trailer that blocks your inside rearview mirror.

questions.question: Is it safe to have a few drinks before driving home?

options.text: Yes, because you will miss rush-hour traffic.
Yes, because it helps you relax and makes you safer.
No, because it can make you a dangerous driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it can make you a dangerous driver.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal. Alcohol slows your reflexes, hurts your judgment, and reduces your alertness. Do not drive after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine work better.
The combination can increase the effects of both.
They have no effect on each other.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and medicine together can increase how much they affect you. For example, one drink with a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks alone.

questions.question: Your headlights must work properly and be correctly adjusted:

options.text: Only when you drive in a city.

questions.explanation: Your headlights are critical for safe driving at night, in rain, in fog, and in tunnels. They must always work properly and be correctly adjusted.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving in bad weather?

options.text: You must change your driving when weather changes suddenly.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Be aware of vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What should you do to ensure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: An arrogant driver is a driver who:

options.text: Drives in a hurry and races other cars.
Does not respect traffic laws or other drivers and pedestrians.

questions.explanation: An arrogant driver rushes and races other cars. They do not respect traffic laws or other drivers and pedestrians. Never race or compete with an arrogant driver.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Slow down when you approach turns on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and return to the missed exit.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: As a motorist, you should:

options.text: Give bicyclists more space than you think they need.
Yield to bicyclists when you cross a bike lane.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are legal vehicles with the same rights as other vehicles. Yield to bicyclists when crossing bike lanes. Give bicyclists plenty of space.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is merging onto the road from the right.

questions.question: Smoking and getting ready to smoke while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up as they pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Move out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up, as this may anger them and increase danger.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
The driver who arrives last has the right-of-way.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave the other drivers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who arrives first goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road may be wet and slippery.
